scope.description: Hand-researched deepening pass for English Best of Game and all nine rows carrying its promo, Winner-stamp, Rocket, Dark evolution, and organized-play branch structure.

sources.title: Local English WoC catalog: Best of Game
Pokemon TCG API v2 set record: Best of Game
Bulbapedia: Best of Game (TCG)

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API model Best of Game with a December 1, 2002 release date.
The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API support a 9-row Best of Game promo-series checklist.
Bulbapedia treats Best of Game as a promotional set tied to Wizards-era organized-play distribution, with Winner-stamped and non-Winner branches as well as jumbo context for selected cards.
The local catalog preserves Best of Game as Pokemon TCG API set id bp and release_family_id en_wotc_best_of_game_20021201, separate from Gym Challenge, BattleZone, jumbo, and later reprint branches.
The local Best of Game attention rows include Dark Venusaur, Rocket's Mewtwo, Rocket's Scizor, Rocket's Sneasel, Dark Ivysaur, Rocket's Hitmonchan, Professor Elm, Electabuzz, and Hitmonchan.

The local Best of Game artist clusters include Ken Sugimori for early competitive staples and Shin-ichi Yoshida for the Dark Ivysaur / Dark Venusaur / Rocket's Mewtwo branch, with K Hoshiba and Katsura Tabata carrying single Rocket rows.

Best of Game matters because it turns tournament participation, winning, and late-Wizards promo distribution into a compact nine-card object: the card is not only a game piece, it is a trace of where competitive Pokemon was being handed to players.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, or agent memory says Best of Game, bp, Winner stamp, Rocket's Mewtwo, Rocket's Scizor, Rocket's Sneasel, Dark Venusaur, jumbo, BattleZone, or Gym Challenge.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Best of Game is a nine-row English promo series under set id bp. Preserve row id, Winner-stamp status, jumbo status, and source release before comparing to Gym Challenge or other branches.
steps: Preserve release_family_id en_wotc_best_of_game_20021201 and Pokemon TCG API set id bp.
Ask for a clear scan of any claimed Winner stamp; do not infer stamp status from the Best of Game row alone.
Ask for physical dimensions or slab/label evidence before treating a copy as jumbo.
Do not collapse Best of Game Rocket's Mewtwo into Gym Challenge Rocket's Mewtwo without naming the release change.
Do not infer price, condition, authenticity, winner status, event provenance, or seller possession from the catalog row alone.

narrative.human_title: The prize table at the edge of Wizards
narrative.why_it_matters: Best of Game feels like a little end-of-era packet. It is only nine rows, but it carries a lot of machinery: Winner stamps, Rocket ownership, Dark evolution, jumbo echoes, and the feeling of cards moving through tournaments rather than booster packs. The set is not trying to be a world. It is a receipt from organized play, with just enough villain shine to make the receipt collectible.
